entries.title: build the histogram-atomic example without --allow-panics
entries.body:
examples/histogram-atomic.ts and the JsonNumber guide snippet now build without --allow-panics. std/threads.ts adds checked twins, atomicI32ArrayChecked and atomicI64ArrayChecked, which return Err for a negative length where the constructors panic. std/json-typed.ts tests its string-field window, removing two slice panic sites. std/net/websocket.ts checks a close frame's reason without the window panic.

The stale-opt-out checks now build each example and snippet both with -o and with --link, and keep an opt-out while either build refuses it for a panic site.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse an RFC a std/ module cites with no vector spec
entries.body:
scripts/rfc-specs.mjs, now part of npm run lint, reads every RFC citation in
std/**/*.ts as text: RFC or RFCs and a number in either case, across a
wrapped comment line, and each number of a list or a range. Each (file, RFC)
pair needs a vector spec of that module (its contract, specs/<n>.md, and a
test/spec/<n>.ts pinning the contract's SHA-256) or a line in
scripts/rfc-unspecified.txt.

The 231 pairs that predate the rule are listed there, and PRE_RULE_SHA256 in
the script pins their set: a line added, swapped or deleted by hand fails,
and --update-baseline, which runs only on the pinned set, is the one way a
line goes. A `cites: <reason>` line is for an RFC a file names without
implementing it; std/crypto/x509.ts's rfc822Name is the first. A listed pair
a spec now covers, or the file no longer cites, fails until its line goes.

CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md ("Picking up a work package"), the orientation and
contracts/README.md now say that a module implementing an RFC lands
spec-first, and that a change to a module with a spec reruns vector's check
and mutate.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
